newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Fortune Oil to invest in China depot.
newsitem.headline: Fortune Oil to invest in China depot.

text.p: Fortune Oil Plc said on Monday it has agreed to invest HK$51 million in new oil depot facilities at Jiangmen, in China's southern Guangdong province.
This is the second investment by the company in oil depots in China, following its HK$34 million investment in a depot in Shantou, expected to be completed by end 1997, Fortune said in a statement.

The Jiangmen facility is expected to be operational in May 1997, with total storage capacity of 40,000 cubic metres, comprising two 10,000 and three 5,000 cubic metre tanks for fuel oil, and one 5,000 cubic metre tank for diesel.
A jetty with capacity to unload up to 3,000-tonne ships would also be built, the company said.
The joint venture depot is 25 percent-owned by Fairy International Ltd, 55 percent by Jiangmen Power Development Co and 20 percent by Haicheng Trading Development Co.

Fairy would act as Fortune Oil's authorised reseller to sell petroleum to the joint venture, and the group will not purchase petroleum products in the open market unless Fortune is unable to supply at competitive prices, the statement said.

Of Fortune's HK$51 million investment, to be funded by a syndicated loan facility, HK$12 million is in a reseller loan to Fairy for a 50 percent share of Fairy's profits from the joint venture and HK$39 million in a direct loan to the joint venture.
The depot will supply 150,000 tonnes per year of fuel oil to the nearby Xi Jiang Power Plant, the company said.
